title: Quantum many-body mixed phase space revealed by hybrid feedback control
authors: Hang Dong, Jie Ren, Andrew Hallam, Han Wang, Zhengyi Cui, Yiren Zou, Junlin Wang, Hekang Li, Qiujiang Guo, Zhen Wang, Lei Ying, Zlatko Papic
abstract: Understanding how complex systems transition between order and chaos is a central challenge of nonequilibrium physics. While weak perturbations of classical integrable systems give rise to a mixed phase space of coexisting regular and chaotic trajectories, analogous behavior in interacting quantum many-body systems has remained elusive. Here we develop and experimentally implement a hybrid quantum-classical feedback protocol that autonomously discovers and stabilizes long-lived regular trajectories in a superconducting quantum processor. Each iteration combines short-time quantum evolution with classical optimization that projects the dynamics back onto a low-entanglement variational manifold, effectively distilling coherence from chaotic evolution. The stabilized trajectories reveal a quantum many-body mixed phase space emerging from nonlinear variational dynamics, without a direct analogue in classical or few-body quantum systems. Our results establish a versatile framework for algorithmic discovery and control of coherent dynamics previously inaccessible to experiment.
summary: The research addresses the challenge of observing mixed phase space dynamics in interacting quantum systems by developing and implementing a hybrid quantum-classical feedback control protocol. This method stabilizes coherent, regular quantum trajectories on superconducting qubits, revealing an emergent quantum many-body mixed phase space structure. It establishes a powerful framework for experimentally controlling and characterizing complex non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The central challenge is understanding how complex interacting quantum many-body systems transition between ordered (regular) and chaotic dynamics, revealing a mixed phase space structure.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that a hybrid quantum-classical feedback protocol can autonomously discover and stabilize long-lived regular trajectories, revealing an emergent quantum many-body mixed phase space distinct from classical analogs.
method: They employ a Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) framework combined with a novel hybrid feedback control loop to project the full quantum evolution onto a low-entanglement variational manifold.
model_or_system: The study uses an interacting spin-1/2 model inspired by the Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) ladder, implemented on a superconducting qubit processor. The dynamics are governed by a complex Hamiltonian involving various couplings ($J_t, J_b, J_{	ext{int}}$).
key_observables: Poincaré sections derived from imbalance measurements ($I_z(t)$), entanglement entropy ($S_E$), and the co-moving imbalance ($	ext{ICM}$).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in regimes where couplings are small relative to inter-leg coupling ($J_e, J_3 \ll J_o$); the analysis also explores the thermodynamic limit ($N	o\infty$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are approximated by restricting the state evolution to a low-dimensional variational manifold $M$, which is an approximation of the full quantum Hilbert space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic circuit setups, 3D visualizations of the variational manifold showing regular vs. chaotic regions, and Poincaré sections derived from imbalance measurements that confirm the coexistence of stable islands and chaotic seas.
paper_structure: The paper develops a hybrid feedback protocol to stabilize dynamics on the variational manifold, using TDVP to derive effective classical equations of motion. Key diagnostics like $I_z(t)$ are used to map out the mixed phase space structure, comparing theoretical predictions with experimental measurements on superconducting qubits.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum simulation techniques (TDVP/variational methods) with fundamental concepts from classical dynamical systems theory (KAM tori, Poincaré sections), providing a concrete pathway to experimentally probe non-equilibrium statistical physics in many-body quantum matter.
